cues.en: If you remember back to our Deep Learning introduction, recurrent neural networks, or RNN's, are good at finding patterns in sequences of data, and predicting what comes next.
cues.zh: 回想深度學習入門，RNN 擅長找出資料序列的模式，預測接下來會發生什麼。

cues.en: Well, some recommendation problems can be thought of in those terms.
cues.zh: 有些推薦問題，也能這樣思考。

cues.en: We call them session-based recommendations.
cues.zh: 稱為工作階段式推薦。

cues.en: Let's give you a couple of examples.
cues.zh: 舉幾個例子。

cues.en: Let's say you're shopping on Amazon or something.
cues.zh: 假設在 Amazon 之類的網站購物。

cues.en: If you're not logged in, then making recommendations to you is really hard!
cues.zh: 如果沒登入，推薦就很難。

cues.en: We don't know who you are, so we don't know what your past history is on the site or what your past interests are.
cues.zh: 不知道你是誰，就不知道網站上的歷史，或過去興趣。

cues.en: We can keep track of your session though as you browse the site using the same browser window.
cues.zh: 但在同一瀏覽器視窗瀏覽時，仍能追蹤工作階段。

cues.en: Perhaps you've decided to learn how to speak Klingon, because for some reason you've decided that would be a useful life skill.
cues.zh: 也許你決定學克林貢語，不知為何覺得是有用的生活技能。

cues.en: In fact it's not, but let's just make it interesting.
cues.zh: 其實不是，但讓例子有趣一點。

cues.en: Perhaps the first book you look at is How to Speak Klingon, so that's the first thing in your clickstream.
cues.zh: 第一本可能看 How to Speak Klingon，這就是點擊流中的第一項。

cues.en: So at this point literally the only thing our recommender system knows about you is that you looked at the book How to Speak Klingon.
cues.zh: 此時，推薦系統唯一知道的，就是你看過 How to Speak Klingon。

cues.en: But at least that's something.
cues.zh: 但至少是個資訊。

cues.en: Maybe you didn't like the reviews on this book or something, so you moved on to another book you found Shakespeare's Hamlet, translated into Klingon, yes, this really exists.
cues.zh: 也許不喜歡書評，轉而找到另一本，克林貢語版莎士比亞《哈姆雷特》，沒錯，真的存在。

cues.en: So at this point, we can say your clickstream consists of these two items, it is a sequence of clicks, one on How to Speak Klingon, and a second on Klingon Hamlet.
cues.zh: 此時，點擊流包含兩個項目，依序點 How to Speak Klingon，再點 Klingon Hamlet。

cues.en: If you wanted to make a recommendation at this point, a reasonable thing would be to try and predict what someone who just viewed these two items, in this order, might look at next.
cues.zh: 若現在要推薦，合理做法，是預測剛依這個順序看過兩項的人，接下來會看什麼。

cues.en: That is, you'd like to make recommendations based on the sequence of things you've looked at previously.
cues.zh: 也就是，根據先前看過項目的序列推薦。

cues.en: Predicting sequences is what RNN's do, which is why they are a natural fit for this sort of problem.
cues.zh: 預測序列正是 RNN 的工作，因此自然適合這種問題。

cues.en: Perhaps the most likely thing for a user to click on next is The Klingon Dictionary, which is of course the definitive reference for the Klingon language.
cues.zh: 也許接下來最可能點 The Klingon Dictionary，當然是克林貢語的權威參考書。

cues.en: Maybe the user clicked on that because our RNN recommended it, and hopefully they then purchase that item and move on with their life.
cues.zh: 也許因 RNN 推薦而點擊，希望接著購買，繼續生活。

cues.en: So this particular session is over, and this session's clickstream consists of these three books.
cues.zh: 這次工作階段就結束，點擊流包含這三本書。

cues.en: There is a dataset called the RecSys Challenge 2015 dataset that contains data exactly like this you can play around with.
cues.zh: 有一個 RecSys Challenge 2015 資料集，包含這樣的資料，可以實驗。

cues.en: Another application of session-based recommendations based on clickstreams is streaming video sites, such as YouTube or Vimeo.
cues.zh: 另一種根據點擊流的工作階段式推薦，應用在 YouTube 或 Vimeo 等串流影片網站。

cues.en: Again, if you're not logged in, all we know is the sequence of videos you watch but we can still use that sequence to recommend what you should watch next.
cues.zh: 同樣，沒登入時，只知道你看的影片序列，但仍能用它推薦下一部。

cues.en: That's the sort of thing RNN's are for.
cues.zh: RNN 正是用來做這類事。

cues.en: Maybe you're watching videos from Sundog Education's amazing YouTube channel, because who doesn't?
cues.zh: 也許你在看 Sundog Education 精彩的 YouTube 頻道，誰不看呢？

cues.en: Anyhow, the sequence of videos you watch from our channel can all be considered part of a clickstream as well, and the problem of recommending what to watch next based on the videos you watched
cues.zh: 總之，觀看我們頻道的影片序列，也能視為點擊流。根據目前工作階段先前看過的影片，

cues.en: previously in your session works exactly the same way as the e-commerce clickstream problem.
cues.zh: 推薦下一部，與電商點擊流問題，運作完全相同。

cues.en: The paper that describes using RNN's for making session-based recommendations has the creative title of session-based recommendations with recurrent neural networks.
cues.zh: 描述以 RNN 做工作階段式推薦的論文，有個很有創意的標題：Session-based Recommendations with Recurrent Neural Networks。

cues.en: You might notice Netflix in the list of authors, but the author actually took a job at Netflix in between producing this work and when it was published.
cues.zh: 可能注意到作者名單有 Netflix，但作者是在完成研究與發表之間，到 Netflix 就職。

cues.en: Netflix didn't really have anything to do with it, but it's a good example of how doing interesting research in recommender systems can land you a job in a company you love.
cues.zh: Netflix 其實沒參與，但這是好例子：有趣的推薦系統研究，可能讓你進入喜歡的公司。

cues.en: You can find a legitimate free copy of this paper on the Internet if you want to go into more depth.
cues.zh: 想深入，可以在網路找到合法免費版本。

cues.en: This paper is just from 2016, and I considered making it a bleeding edge alert topic because it is so new, but really, it's just some minor twists on RNN which are by now a proven technology.
cues.zh: 這篇是 2016 年的，我原本想放進前沿研究提醒，因為很新，但其實只是對已驗證的 RNN，做一些小調整。

cues.en: The world of Deep Learning is moving so quickly, that research from 2016 really can't be considered bleeding edge, or even leading edge at this point.
cues.zh: 深度學習發展太快，2016 年研究，此時已不能稱為尚待驗證前沿，甚至不能稱最先進。

cues.en: We're in exciting times here.
cues.zh: 我們正處於令人興奮的年代。

cues.en: Mostly, the paper concerns itself with how to tweak RNN's to work well with session-based clickstream data.
cues.zh: 論文主要談，如何調整 RNN，適合工作階段點擊流資料。

cues.en: If you remember, RNN's are rather complicated beasts, instead of simple neurons, they depend on more complex structures such as LSTM, or in our case GRU's gated recurrent units.
cues.zh: 記得，RNN 相當複雜，不是簡單神經元，而是依賴 LSTM，或這裡的 GRU 閘控循環單元等複雜結構。

cues.en: This gives the network an internal hidden state within each unit that must be maintained.
cues.zh: 每個單元，都有必須維護的內部隱藏狀態。

cues.en: GRU gates learn when and by how much to update that hidden state within each unit.
cues.zh: GRU 的閘門，學習何時、更新多少隱藏狀態。

cues.en: Because the paper relies on GRU's with some customizations for the recommendation problem, its technique is sometimes referred to as GRU4Rec.
cues.zh: 因為論文依賴 GRU，並為推薦問題客製化，因此有時稱為 GRU4Rec。

cues.en: A simplified view of the architecture looks like this, this represents the processing of a single event in the clickstream.
cues.zh: 簡化架構像這樣，代表處理點擊流的單一事件。

cues.en: We start with the item that was just viewed encoded as 1-of-N, and that goes into an embedding layer, and that in turn leads into multiple GRU layers.
cues.zh: 先把剛看過項目，編成 N 選一，送入 Embedding，再進多個 GRU 層。

cues.en: We've represented it as a single block here in the interest of space, but in practice there can be many GRU layers in the middle here.
cues.zh: 為了空間，只畫成一個區塊，但實務上，中間可以有很多 GRU 層。

cues.en: There can also be many feed-forward layers after the GRU layers, these are just more traditional neural network layers that don't involve fancy GRU's.
cues.zh: GRU 後也能有多個前饋層，就是不含複雜 GRU 的傳統神經網路層。

cues.en: And finally we get scores on the all of the items, from which we can select the items the deep network thinks is most likely to be viewed next in the clickstream.
cues.zh: 最後，得到所有項目分數，選出深度網路認為點擊流中，最可能接著看的項目。

cues.en: There are a few other twists on RNN's that the authors made for the recommender use case.
cues.zh: 作者還為推薦用途，對 RNN 做了其他調整。

cues.en: They feed data into the network in a different way than you would, for example, feed in words from a sentence.
cues.zh: 輸入資料的方式，不同於輸入句子中的詞。

cues.en: Basically, multiple sessions are grouped together, and all of their first items are fed in together, then all of their second items, and so forth.
cues.zh: 基本上，將多個工作階段分組，所有第一項一起輸入，再所有第二項，依此類推。

cues.en: They call this session-parallel mini-batches.
cues.zh: 稱為工作階段平行小批次。

cues.en: They also sample the output, because in most recommender systems there are a large number of items, and it's computationally prohibitive to look at every item every time when you want a recommendation right now,
cues.zh: 也對輸出取樣，因為多數推薦系統，項目很多；要根據使用者剛點的東西，立刻推薦，

cues.en: based on what the user just clicked on.
cues.zh: 每次查看每個項目的運算成本，難以負擔。

cues.en: Finally, they experiment with specific loss functions for training, and settled on two of them, Bayesian Personalized Ranking, or BPR for short, and TOP1, which is a new loss function
cues.zh: 最後，實驗特定訓練損失函數，選定兩個：貝氏個人化排序，簡稱 BPR，以及 TOP1，作者

cues.en: the authors developed specifically for this application.
cues.zh: 專為這個應用開發的新損失函數。

cues.en: Now, one thing I've learned repeatedly in my career is that simpler solutions tend to be better.
cues.zh: 職涯中，我一再學到，簡單解法通常比較好。

cues.en: And GRU4Rec is far from simple.
cues.zh: 而 GRU4Rec 遠非簡單。

cues.en: Before I would adopt a technology like this, I would really have to be convinced that it offers substantially better results than simpler alternatives do.
cues.zh: 採用前，必須確信它比簡單替代方案，產生明顯更好結果。

cues.en: There are other ways of making recommendations based on session data, this problem was around long before RNN's were.
cues.zh: 還有其他方式，根據工作階段推薦，這問題遠早於 RNN。

cues.en: You can just treat the items in someone's session just like somebody's set of past movie ratings or whatever, and use item-based KNN or collaborative filtering to recommend things that are similar to the stuff
cues.zh: 可以把工作階段項目，當成某人的歷史電影評分集合，用項目式 KNN 或協同過濾，推薦與他已點過東西

cues.en: they clicked on already.
cues.zh: 相似的項目。

cues.en: That doesn't take the order of the clicks into account, but in practice that information isn't always that important.
cues.zh: 雖沒考慮點擊順序，但實務上，這資訊不一定重要。

cues.en: And if you dig into the paper's results, they were able to get slightly better results from RNN's than they did from item-based KNN, but it wasn't a dramatic difference.
cues.zh: 深入論文結果，RNN 比項目式 KNN 略好，但差異不大。

cues.en: Nor was it evaluated with online, real people, so more experiments would have to be run to say if it's really a superior approach or not.
cues.zh: 也沒有線上真實使用者評估，所以需要更多實驗，才能說是否真的更好。

cues.en: There is a real cost to deploying something like this into a production system.
cues.zh: 部署到正式系統，有真實成本。

cues.en: If it starts producing bad recommendations, who will understand the algorithm well enough to be able to tune it and correct it?
cues.zh: 如果開始產生差推薦，誰能充分理解演算法，調整、修正？

cues.en: How much hardware will it take to power a system this large and complex, and what happens when that hardware breaks?
cues.zh: 這麼大、這麼複雜的系統，需要多少硬體？硬體故障怎麼辦？

cues.en: How long does it take to produce recommendations for a given session, and how does that affect the page render time for the website it's integrated into?
cues.zh: 為某工作階段產生推薦要多久？會如何影響整合網站的頁面呈現時間？

cues.en: That last concern could be enough to kill the project in itself.
cues.zh: 最後這一點，本身就可能讓專案被取消。

cues.en: My point is that systems like this are definitely worth learning about and evaluating, especially since Deep Learning seems to be where all the current research is heading and we want to take advantage of that.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，這類系統絕對值得學習、評估，尤其目前研究似乎都朝深度學習前進，我們想利用進展。

cues.en: But there are practical considerations that must be made, and a complex system should never replace a simpler one that works just as well.
cues.zh: 但有實務考量，複雜系統，絕不該取代同樣有效的簡單系統。

cues.en: You're the one that will be woken up at 2 a.m.
cues.zh: 記得，凌晨兩點被叫醒的人，

cues.en: when something goes wrong with it, remember.
cues.zh: 會是你，因為系統出了問題。
